sourceFacts.fact: Many infantile periocular haemangiomas can be observed, but those threatening vision need treatment.
Propranolol is a first-line treatment for haemangiomas needing systemic therapy; treatment selection and monitoring are supervised.

layoutSpecification: Title 'Haemangioma: protect developing vision'. Draw a clear two-branch path beginning at a generic small ochre cluster of round tokens on the LEFT labelled 'Infantile haemangioma' (not a realistic birthmark or blood vessel). Branch UP along teal path to a clear square window icon, label 'Vision safe', then a calendar icon labelled 'Monitor'. Branch DOWN along ochre path to a square window partly obscured by a plain ochre shade, label 'Vision threatened', then a clinician badge and an unmeasured plain medicine bottle labelled 'Specialist treatment'. Small line under bottle 'Propranolol may be used'. Window is only a metaphor for visual function. No actual eyelid, eyeball, lesion photograph, optic pathway, dosage or claim all haemangiomas need medication. Arrows flow from assessment to appropriate branch.
